name: Pencil Marks
description: The notation players actually think in. A cell can hold a set of candidates as well as an answer, and the two are different states rather than the same field styled differently — committing an answer must not silently discard the working that led to it, because undoing a wrong commit should restore the marks. Auto-elimination is offered and is off by default: a solver that removes candidates for you is doing the deduction the puzzle exists to ask for, and it should be an accessibility choice rather than the standard experience.

inputs.name: autoEliminate
inputs.description: Whether placing a value clears that candidate from its peers. Off by default: this is the deduction the puzzle is asking for.

inputs.name: preserveMarksOnCommit
inputs.description: Whether marks survive committing an answer, so an undo restores the working.

outputs.name: markedCellCount
outputs.description: Cells carrying at least one candidate.
